children: SalamAir, Oman’s low-cost carrier, has opened ticket sales for a new service to Copenhagen via Baghdad, with flights scheduled to begin on November 15, 2026.

Operating under fifth-freedom traffic rights on the Baghdad–Copenhagen sector, the route will connect Muscat, Baghdad and the Danish capital, while allowing Iraqi passengers to book direct flights between Baghdad and Copenhagen.

SalamAir said the service will expand affordable international travel, strengthen connectivity between the Middle East and Northern Europe, and support leisure, business and visiting-friends-and-relatives traffic.

Steven Allen, Chief Commercial Officer of SalamAir, said: “Copenhagen is the ninth new destination added to SalamAir’s network for 2026, reflecting the pace of our expansion and our focus on developing commercially promising markets. Operating twice weekly, the service creates an important new connection between Oman, Iraq and Northern Europe, serving demand between Baghdad and Copenhagen while offering travellers more affordable options to and from Oman. It will also generate new passenger flows across our network and create further opportunities for tourism, trade and business exchange, in line with the objectives of Oman Vision 2040.”

title: ZAWYA: SalamAir expands European network with Muscat–Copenhagen service via Baghdad
